alternates.description: VE Option 1: Mechanically attached system (instead of fully adhered) — save $42,000
VE Option 2: Reduced insulation — single-layer R-30 instead of two-layer staggered — save $18,000 (contractor NOT RECOMMENDED)
VE Option 3: Upgrade 60 mil to 80 mil TPO with 30-year NDL — add $38,000
VE Option 4: Upgrade R-30 to R-38 insulation — add $24,000
VE Option 5: Combined (mech-attached + 80 mil + R-38, no cover board) — net add $12,000
VE Option 6: Phased installation across fiscal years for CCA treatment (schedule impact)

exclusions_declared: Major steel deck repairs exceeding $10,000 allowance
Major wood deck replacement exceeding $10,000 allowance
Replacement of damaged roof drains or leaders
Work outside standard hours (7 AM - 6 PM weekdays)
Hazardous material abatement beyond minor handling
Third-party testing/inspection beyond our testing allowance
clarifications: Ponding correction based on $20,000 tapered-insulation allowance; final quantity TBD at removal
Deck allowances ($10k steel + $10k wood) assumed sufficient for typical conditions; extras via change order
ACM testing allowance included; major abatement would be extra
HVAC shutdowns assumed to be schedulable for weekends; weekday shutdowns require 72-hr notice
Owner to provide temperature monitoring equipment in warehouse
Cover board included in base bid but can be removed if VE Option 5 is selected
Building permits typically owner responsibility; can be arranged for separate fee

substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Contractor asserts mechanically attached system is acceptable for a single-storey, 28-ft industrial building with parapet walls in Mississauga; warranty and service life comparable (25-28 years vs 30+ years), savings $42,000. Proposed as optional VE — base bid remains fully-adhered.

substitutions_proposed.spec_item: Cover board (1/4" gypsum or HD polyiso) per RFP
substitutions_proposed.substitute_offered: No cover board (under VE Option 5 only)
substitutions_proposed.equivalence_justification: Contractor states Carlisle and Firestone do not require cover board with mechanically attached assembly. Only applies if VE Option 5 accepted. Base bid retains 1/4" gypsum cover board.

materials_system.manufacturer: Carlisle / Firestone / GAF (multiple certifications held; specific manufacturer for this project not named in base bid)
materials_system.system_name: TPO single-ply, 60 mil, fully-adhered with R-30 polyiso (two-layer staggered) and 1/4" gypsum cover board

warranty_offered.certification_program: Carlisle Syntec Master Installer; Firestone Premier Contractor; GAF Master Elite

references_provided.project_name: Amazon Fulfillment Centre YHM1, Hamilton ON

technical_approach.narrative: Three-phase plan on 85,000 sqft occupied pharma-warehouse. Phase 1: office wing (5,100 sqft, days 1-18). Phase 2: NW main (20,000 sqft, days 19-52). Phase 3: SE main incl. ponding areas (25,000 sqft, days 53-90). Max 10,000 sqft exposed at any time (below 15,000 sqft RFP limit), daily watertight by 5 PM, weekend reinforced tarps with weighted edges + secondary drainage, 2 coordination meetings/week, 72-hr HVAC shutdown notice.
technical_approach.tear_off_staging_plan: Three-phase sequenced staging described (office wing first, then NW main, then SE main). Maximum exposed area capped at 10,000 sqft. No dumpster placement, lift strategy, or adjacent-property protection detail provided.
technical_approach.weather_protection_plan: Each phase watertight by 5 PM daily. Weekend protection uses reinforced tarps with weighted edges and secondary drainage. No explicit forecast-monitoring protocol provided.
technical_approach.fall_protection_plan: COR-certified; fall protection training for all workers (updated annually); dedicated safety coordinator for projects >75,000 sqft; CRSP-certified Safety Coordinator. No site-specific parapet/perimeter fall-arrest plan, no named anchor points.
technical_approach.waste_disposal_plan: Complete roof removal and legal disposal included. Lead flashing separated and disposed of as hazardous waste. No recycling commitments stated.

wsib_clearance.evidence: Bid §INSURANCE COVERAGE cites WSIB Account #7890123-45; attachments list 'WSIB Clearance Certificate' and 'WSIB Experience Rating Letter (0.81)'. RFP §5.1.1.
wsib_clearance.notes: Good-standing text not quoted in the bid body; standard condition for online re-verification at clearances.wsib.ca applies per fixture 04 §1.4.

cgl_insurance.evidence: Bid §INSURANCE COVERAGE: CGL $5,000,000 per occurrence — meets RFP §5.1.2 minimum. Bid does NOT explicitly state owner named as additional insured nor the completed-operations tail (RFP requires 2 yrs). COI attached per attachments list but not quoted.
cgl_insurance.notes: Owner to verify COI endorsement shows Tenebrus Capital as additional insured and 2-yr completed-ops coverage per RFP §5.1.2.

bid_bond.evidence: RFP §9.2 requires 50% performance + 50% L&M bonds (no bid-bond % stated in RFP). Bid declares bonding capacity up to $5M per project — comfortably above $578k project value. Consent of surety not explicitly attached.
bid_bond.notes: RFP did not require a bid bond; bonding capacity declaration satisfies surety-capacity check. Consent of surety should be confirmed pre-award per fixture 04 §5.

working_at_heights.evidence: Bid §SAFETY PROGRAM: 'Fall protection training for all workers (updated annually)' and COR certification. RFP §5.1 / fixture 04 §3 (O. Reg. 297/13).
working_at_heights.notes: Current WAH training cards should be verified at contract signing.

addenda_acknowledgment.evidence: Bid does not contain a Form of Tender section explicitly acknowledging addenda. No addenda numbers cited. RFP mandatory per §5.1.
addenda_acknowledgment.notes: Owner to confirm addenda acknowledgment before award.

non_collusion_declaration.evidence: No non-collusion declaration found in the bid body or the attachments list. RFP mandatory.
non_collusion_declaration.notes: Likely submitted under separate Form of Tender not included in markdown excerpt; owner to confirm.

site_visit.evidence: Cover letter: 'We attended the mandatory site visit on March 25, 2026'. RFP §6.4 / §8.1.

minimum_years_in_business.evidence: Cover letter: 'Founded in 2012' — 14 years in business as of 2026. Closing remarks: '14 years in business'. RFP §5.1.3 minimum 10 years.

minimum_similar_projects.evidence: Four references provided (Amazon 185k sqft 2024; Magnotta 92k sqft 2023; Prologis 145k sqft 2025; Apotex 78k sqft 2024). All are commercial roof replacements within last 5 years. RFP §5.1.4 minimum 3.
minimum_similar_projects.notes: Reference values were not stated in CAD, so the 0.5×-2× comparable-value test cannot be strictly validated; however, roof-area and scope profiles are plausibly comparable. Apotex is the strongest comparator (78k sqft, temperature-sensitive pharma — near-identical to subject).

red_flags.description: CGL coverage: owner-as-additional-insured endorsement and 2-year completed-operations tail not explicitly confirmed in bid narrative.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §INSURANCE COVERAGE lists CGL $5M but is silent on additional-insured endorsement and completed-ops years.

red_flags.description: Addenda acknowledgment and non-collusion declaration not evidenced in the submitted bid text.
red_flags.evidence: Neither item appears in the bid narrative nor in the attachments list.

red_flags.description: Reference project values not stated; comparability by 0.5×-2× subject-value test cannot be confirmed.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §REFERENCES lists four projects with sqft but omits contract value.

red_flags.description: RFP requires total_system_ndl warranty; bid offers '20-year NDL warranty on TPO membrane' — appears to be a membrane-scope NDL, not a total-system NDL covering the full assembly (insulation, flashings, labour). A specific manufacturer system-warranty program is not named for the base bid.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §WARRANTY (BASE BID): 'Manufacturer Warranty: 20-year NDL warranty on TPO membrane'. No named Platinum/Red Shield/Sopra-Garantie Mammouth program attached for base bid.

red_flags.description: Workmanship warranty is 2 years — meets RFP minimum but below market median of 5 years for a complex occupied pharma-warehouse project with 47 penetrations.
Specific membrane manufacturer for the base bid is not named. Contractor lists three certifications (Carlisle, Firestone, GAF) but does not commit to a single product data line for the 60 mil TPO.
red_flags.citation: fixture 02 §4 mis-matched components voids system warranty
red_flags.evidence: Bid §MANUFACTURER CERTIFICATIONS lists three; base bid section does not name the manufacturer to be installed.

red_flags.description: Wind-uplift design basis (CSA A123.21 or FM 1-29) not stated anywhere in the bid. Single-ply commercial roof, 28 ft, with 47 penetrations requires an explicit uplift design reference.
red_flags.evidence: Bid narrative discusses mechanically-attached vs adhered trade-off under VE Option 1 but never cites a wind-uplift design standard.

red_flags.description: Fall-protection approach is stated generically (COR, WAH training, safety coordinator) but no site-specific plan naming anchor points, parapet/perimeter detail, or CSA Z91 anchor compliance is provided.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §SAFETY PROGRAM describes program-level commitments only.

red_flags.description: VE Option 5 removes cover board from a TPO-over-polyiso assembly. Removing the cover board over polyiso voids most manufacturer system warranties and creates a long-term performance defect (board-joint telegraphing, membrane puncture). Contractor's blanket claim that 'mechanically attached does not require cover board per Carlisle and Firestone' is not supported by current manufacturer guidelines for system-warranted assemblies.
red_flags.citation: fixture 02 §4 cover board requirement; CRCA best practice
red_flags.evidence: Bid VE Option 5: 'Remove cover board (not required with mechanically attached assembly per manufacturer)'.

red_flags.description: VE Option 1 (mechanically attached) proposed as 'ACCEPTABLE' but equivalence justification is thin — site-specific wind uplift design is not provided, and Ontario TPO wind-event losses correlate with mech-attached systems.
red_flags.evidence: Bid VE Option 1: 'wind uplift risk is moderate. Mechanically attached systems are widely used in similar applications.'

red_flags.description: Bid excludes 'work outside standard hours (7 AM - 6 PM weekdays)' — but also commits to 72-hr weekend HVAC shutdowns. Ambiguity about premium for any after-hours or weekend roofing labour that the phasing plan may require.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §EXCLUSIONS item 6 vs §PHASING PLAN weekend protection + §CLARIFICATIONS item 5.

red_flags.description: Crew size not stated and mobilization-days-after-award not stated; 90-day duration on 85,000 sqft occupied building with three phases depends on crew resourcing that is not quantified.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §PROJECT TEAM lists PM/Supervisor/Safety/4 installers but does not specify total crew deployed.

red_flags.description: Bid explicitly excludes replacement of damaged roof drains or leaders; RFP scope included 'tapered insulation or added drains' to resolve ponding. Potential scope gap if drain addition becomes the preferred ponding-correction path.
red_flags.evidence: Bid §EXCLUSIONS item 3 vs RFP included_items 'Tapered insulation or added drains'.

extraction_notes: Base bid explicitly stated before HST: '$578,000 (before HST)'. HST $75,140 listed separately.

Specific TPO membrane manufacturer for base bid was not named — contractor holds three certifications (Carlisle, Firestone, GAF) but did not commit to one. Owner should require manufacturer + product line declared at bid clarification.

Warranty type recorded as `ndl` (not `total_system_ndl`) because bid says '20-year NDL warranty on TPO membrane' — scope is the membrane, not the total system, and no named Platinum/Red Shield/Sopra-Garantie program is attached for the base bid. VE Option 3 upgrades to 30-year NDL but still not explicitly total_system_ndl.
Reference contract values not provided in bid; comparability test uses roof-area and scope profile proxy only. Apotex (78k sqft, temperature-sensitive pharma, 2024) is the strongest direct analogue.
CGL additional-insured endorsement and completed-operations-years tail were not quoted in the bid narrative; COI is attached but not reproduced. Owner to read COI endorsement directly.

Addenda acknowledgment and non-collusion declaration were not found in the bid body — likely submitted under a separate Form of Tender not included in the markdown excerpt. Owner to verify before award.
Wind-uplift design basis (CSA A123.21 or FM 1-29) not stated anywhere in the bid.
Crew size and mobilization-days-after-award not stated numerically.
Unit prices (deck per bf, insulation per sqft per R, flashing per lf) not provided — all deck/ponding handled via lump-sum allowances.

VE Option 5's claim that cover board is not required with a mechanically attached TPO assembly is contestable — most manufacturer system warranties still require a cover board over polyiso. Flagged as critical substitutions red flag.

sub_factors.name: Tear-off & staging
sub_factors.rationale: Three-phase sequenced staging with max 10,000 sqft exposed (below 15k RFP cap); no dumpster placement, lift strategy, or adjacent-property protection detail.

sub_factors.name: Weather protection / dry-in
sub_factors.rationale: Daily watertight by 5 PM per phase, weekend reinforced tarps with weighted edges and secondary drainage; no explicit forecast-monitoring protocol.

sub_factors.name: Fall protection & safety
sub_factors.rationale: COR certification, WAH training, CRSP coordinator stated — program-level only; no site-specific plan, no named anchor points or parapet/perimeter detail.

sub_factors.name: Waste / environmental / logistics
sub_factors.rationale: Complete removal and legal disposal, lead flashing separated as hazardous; no recycling commitments (DSA not required — building 1998).

sub_factors.name: Quality control / inspection protocol
sub_factors.rationale: Coordination meetings referenced but no in-progress QC checkpoints or scheduled manufacturer inspection tied to NDL warranty requirements.

technical_approach.summary: Phased occupied-site plan with solid dry-in commitments but generic fall-protection and thin QC/inspection protocol.

sub_factors.name: Warranty type (vs RFP requirement)
sub_factors.rationale: 20-year NDL on membrane only — falls short of RFP-required total_system_ndl (named system program); recorded at NDL tier per rubric ladder.

sub_factors.name: Warranty years vs RFP minimum
sub_factors.rationale: 20-year manufacturer warranty meets RFP minimum of 20 years; does not exceed.

sub_factors.name: Installer certification at claimed warranty tier
sub_factors.rationale: Multiple top-tier certifications (Carlisle Master Installer, Firestone Premier, GAF Master Elite) aligned with NDL warranty tier claimed.

sub_factors.name: Workmanship warranty years
sub_factors.rationale: 2-year workmanship warranty — meets RFP minimum but below 5-year market median.

sub_factors.name: Materials quality
sub_factors.rationale: 60 mil TPO (meets spec), R-30 two-layer staggered polyiso, 1/4" gypsum cover board — meets industry standard, does not exceed.

warranty_materials.summary: NDL warranty on membrane only falls short of total_system_ndl requirement; certifications strong but workmanship and material tier are baseline.

sub_factors.name: Count of comparable references
sub_factors.rationale: 4 references (Amazon, Magnotta, Prologis, Apotex) — all commercial, within 5 yrs; values not stated so comparability strictly by scope/area proxy (Apotex 78k sqft strongest analogue).

sub_factors.name: Recency of most-recent comparable reference
sub_factors.rationale: Most-recent comparable is Prologis Park 407 (2025) — under 1 year old.

sub_factors.name: Verifiability
sub_factors.rationale: Contacts and completion year provided on all references; contract values missing on every reference.

experience_references.summary: Four recent commercial references including a near-identical pharma analogue; contract values missing limit verifiability.

sub_factors.name: Years in business
sub_factors.rationale: 14 years in business (founded 2012) — falls in 10-14 yr band.

sub_factors.name: Manufacturer certification at or above warranty tier claimed
sub_factors.rationale: Top-tier program (GAF Master Elite) plus Carlisle Master Installer and Firestone Premier — multiple, including a top-tier program.

sub_factors.name: Skilled Trades C of Q crew
sub_factors.rationale: Certificate of Qualification roofer count not stated in bid.

sub_factors.name: Industry membership
sub_factors.rationale: Not a CRCA member; no regional/provincial association cited.

qualifications_certifications.summary: Top-tier GAF Master Elite plus Carlisle/Firestone credentials and 14 years in business; no CRCA membership and crew C of Q count not disclosed.

sub_factors.name: Timeline realism vs scope
sub_factors.rationale: Detailed three-phase sequencing with day ranges (1-18 office, 19-52 NW, 53-90 SE) and specific sqft per phase — realistic for 85,000 sqft occupied site.

sub_factors.name: Crew adequacy
sub_factors.rationale: Crew size not stated numerically; project team lists PM/supervisor/safety/4 installers but total deployed crew not quantified.

sub_factors.name: Mobilization and completion dates vs RFP
sub_factors.rationale: Substantial completion 2026-07-30 meets RFP target; mobilization days after award not stated.

sub_factors.name: Occupied-building accommodation
sub_factors.rationale: Named tenant-coordination plan: 2 coordination meetings/week, 72-hr HVAC shutdown notice, weekend scheduling for weekday shutdowns, daily watertight by 5 PM.

schedule.summary: Detailed three-phase sequencing with strong tenant-coordination plan; crew size and mobilization-days-after-award undisclosed.

strengths: Top-tier manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, Carlisle Master Installer, Firestone Premier) with 14 yrs in business
Detailed three-phase sequencing for occupied pharma-warehouse with 72-hr HVAC coordination and daily watertight commitments
Four commercial references within 5 years, including Apotex pharma as a near-identical scope analogue
weaknesses: Warranty is membrane-only NDL, not the total_system_ndl the RFP requires; no named manufacturer system-warranty program for the base bid
Wind-uplift design basis absent, fall-protection plan only program-level, crew size and mobilization-days-after-award not quantified
scoring_rationale.differentiator: Stacked top-tier manufacturer certifications (including GAF Master Elite) paired with a disciplined three-phase occupied-site plan — but warranty scope and base-bid manufacturer commitment are the catch.
